title: TKMS Closes Israel Submarine Line as Italy Opens $5.14B Tank Tender and Baykar K2 Lands in Pakistan
subhead: Germany's TKMS caps its Dolphin-class era with Israel while chasing Indian, Canadian and Gulf submarine deals; Italy launches a 5.14 billion euro next-generation tank procurement; and Pakistan becomes the first customer of Turkey's 2,000km-class Baykar K2 strike drone. Separately, a GAO report puts US public shipyard modernization above $200 billion.

sections.heading: TKMS Closes Dolphin Chapter and Pivots to India, Canada and the Gulf
sections.body:
TKMS has delivered the final boat of its Dolphin-class programme to Israel, with INS Drakon arriving in Haifa after a largely submerged, secretive voyage of several weeks, according to the Israeli business daily Calcalist. At over 70 metres and 2,600 tonnes, it is the heaviest vessel in Israel's fleet and carries ten torpedo tubes, though full operational readiness is still months away while Israeli systems are fitted on site.

The closure of the Dolphin line is a pivot point rather than a retreat. Germany's ambassador to India, Jasper Wieck, said on Wednesday that Berlin could sign the bilateral government agreement underpinning India's Project 75(I) at any time — a plan that would have TKMS build six submarines in India with Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, though New Delhi has yet to grant final approval. In Canada, Ottawa has named TKMS preferred bidder for a fleet renewal covering as many as twelve boats, with a regular bilateral strategic dialogue planned. In the Middle East, TKMS signed a memorandum of understanding with the UAE's EDGE Group in Munich targeting undersea infrastructure.

TKMS subsidiary TKMS ATLAS UK also won a British Ministry of Defence contract for the Next Generation Countermeasure torpedo-defence system.
sections.whyItMatters: Western submarine industrial capacity is consolidating around a shrinking set of yards. TKMS closing one customer line while bidding for three new ones signals that submarine demand now outruns supply — and that Germany is willing to build locally in customer countries (India) to win orders.

sections.heading: Italy Opens 5.14 Billion Euro Tender for Next-Generation Main Battle Tank
sections.body:
Italy's Ministry of Defence has launched a tender worth approximately 5.14 billion euros for a next-generation main battle tank and variants, recorded in the database of the National Anti-Corruption Authority (ANAC), according to marketscreener/ BusinessAM reporting. The project, the New Main Battle Tank (NMBT), is a Leonardo–Rheinmetall collaboration through their Leonardo Rheinmetall Military Vehicles (LRMV) joint venture, agreed in October 2024 on a 50:50 basis, with 60% of production — testing, final assembly and logistics — in Italy. Rheinmetall manages the platform; Leonardo handles armament and electronics.

The design is influenced by the Panther KF51, adapted to Italian needs. The concept shown at Eurosatory in June used a new turret on a Leopard 2A4 chassis; production models will use a redesigned chassis. Armament is a 120mm smoothbore gun with a 20-round autoloader and an option to upgrade to 130mm, plus a remotely operated 30mm cannon capable of engaging drones — and the demonstrator showed the ability to fire loitering munitions.

Italy needs roughly 132 tanks to replace the ageing C1 Ariete fleet, with deliveries expected after 2027 and completion by 2038, part of a broader 8.2 billion euro land programme. The tender does not yet name a contractor, unit count or delivery schedule.
sections.whyItMatters: European main battle tank demand is being rebuilt around new designs after decades of neglect. The NMBT's drone-firing and counter-drone features show that tanks are being reconceived as anti-drone platforms — a direct lesson absorbed from Ukraine.

sections.heading: Pakistan Inducts Turkey's 2,000km Baykar K2 Kamikaze Drone
sections.body:
Pakistan has inducted Turkey's Baykar K2 long-range kamikaze UAV, potentially becoming its first known export customer, according to Defence Security Asia. The drone appeared in a Pakistan Air Force promotional film. Baykar advertises a range above 2,000km with an approximately 200kg warhead, autonomous navigation and swarm functionality — substantially heavier than conventional Shahed-type one-way attack drones.

No official confirmation yet exists on Pakistan's K2 fleet size, contract value, delivery schedule or basing. But even limited induction extends Pakistan's unmanned reach into strategic-range conventional attack, potentially threatening airbases, command centres, radar installations and logistics hubs without exposing manned aircraft. Unlike Pakistan's ballistic missiles — several of which carry nuclear delivery associations — a long-range kamikaze UAV offers a conventional strike rung that stays below the nuclear threshold.

The K2 integrates with Pakistan's existing Bayraktar TB2 and AKINCI fleets. The report also notes Turkey's role in Pakistan's defence-industrial ecosystem has grown from supplying individual drones to research cooperation, jointly developed loitering munitions and counter-drone systems.
sections.whyItMatters: This is a case of drone proliferation shifting conventional deep-strike balances in South Asia. It also underscores Turkey's emergence as a full-spectrum unmanned systems exporter, able to shape the strategic calculus of a nuclear-armed state.

sections.heading: GAO: US Public Shipyard Modernization Could Top $200 Billion
sections.body:
A Government Accountability Office report released September 25 finds the US Navy's effort to rebuild and modernize its four public shipyards could cost more than $200 billion and take more than 50 additional years. The Navy launched the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) in 2018 to fix deteriorating facilities and capability gaps at the yards that maintain and modernize nuclear-powered carriers and submarines. GAO found the programme will take years longer and cost far more than originally anticipated — a jump from roughly $21 billion in 2018 estimates, per reporting by WorkBoat and AInvest.

Environmental issues and scope changes added work. GAO called for regular reviews of the programme's requirements, costs and risks.
sections.whyItMatters: Submarine and carrier availability depends on these yards. A 50-year, $200 billion overrun is a bottleneck on US naval power projection that no amount of new construction can outrun — it constrains how many hulls the US can actually keep at sea.

sections.heading: Hanwha Restructures US Operations Around Land, Sea and Missiles
sections.body:
South Korea's Hanwha Group is consolidating all US defence activity under Hanwha Defense USA, according to The Herald Business. Last month it signed a US Army contract to supply prototype K9 wheeled self-propelled howitzers — designated K9MH — under the Mobile Tactical Cannon programme, and separately announced a large ammunition production facility in Arkansas. In Opelika, Alabama, it is setting up a facility to assemble, integrate and test K9MH prototypes.

The scope is widening beyond land. Hanwha Systems disclosed it will sell its entire 60% stake in Hanwha Philly Shipyard to Hanwha Defense USA for 325.1 billion won ($239 million), closing October 31, bringing land and maritime defence under one US entity. Hanwha Defense USA is also bidding for Austal USA. Recent US hires include CEO Michael Coulter, shipbuilding president and retired US Navy rear admiral Tom Anderson, and COO Mike Smith.
sections.whyItMatters: Korean primes are no longer just exporters to the US — they are buying local industrial capacity and embedding US leadership. This is defense-industrial localization as a market-entry strategy, and it puts Hanwha directly into US shipbuilding.

sections.heading: Taiwan Presses Its Case as Trump Holds Arms Package in Abeyance
sections.body:
Following the three-day Trump–Xi summit in Washington, Taiwan's Deputy Foreign Minister Francois Wu told reporters in Taipei that arming Taiwan and keeping its semiconductor industry contributing to the world are in US national interest, per Reuters/CNBC. Xi told Trump he hoped the US would adhere to the 'correct position' of opposing Taiwan independence. Trump, who in May said he was holding a Taiwan arms package in abeyance, has made no public comment on Taiwan since the summit.

Separately, four Republican senators had called on the administration to release more than $15 billion in stalled national security assistance for Taiwan, as Reuters reported on September 23. US Senate Democrats criticized the summit as prioritizing pageantry over substance on AI, trade, critical minerals and Taiwan weapons.
sections.whyItMatters: The question of whether Washington trades arms deliveries for a diplomatic reset with Beijing is now openly contested inside the US Congress. Taiwan's defence posture, and the semiconductor leverage tied to it, sits at the center of that debate.

bottomLine: Today's developments point the same direction from different angles: submarine and armor industrial capacity is being reorganized around a handful of Western and Asian primes, and demand continues to outrun supply. TKMS closes the Dolphin line while bidding for India, Canada and Gulf work; Italy opens a 5.14 billion euro tank tender with drone-fighting features; Pakistan becomes the first known customer of Turkey's 2,000km Baykar K2; and GAO warns that fixing the US's own shipyards could cost over $200 billion and half a century. Meanwhile Washington's pending Taiwan arms package remains frozen behind the Trump–Xi channel, with Congress pushing back. The throughline is that industrial base and political will — not design concepts — are deciding what militaries can actually field.
sources: Defence Security Asia, Reuters, CNBC, marketscreener/BusinessAM, The Herald Business, WorkBoat, AInvest, Calcalist (via ad-hoc-news), Defence Security Asia
